key_insight: Reference-policy KL can keep influencing group updates even when rewards are clipped, canceled, or identical, so the paper argues for calibrating KL with within-group relative drift instead of adding it as a separate regularizer.
engineering_relevance: For RLHF-style group policy optimization, ZCPO offers a more stable way to control policy drift and avoid length- or token-level KL imbalances that can distort learning.
method: Analyzes seven KL–reward failure modes in group policy optimization, including residual updates, length imbalance, token concentration, and sampling noise.
Uses conditional KL to measure relative drift within each group and calibrate reward coefficients accordingly.
Integrates the calibrated coefficients into the base surrogate to form Zero-Sum Calibrated Policy Optimization (ZCPO).
evidence_signal: The abstract reports mathematical reasoning experiments and ablations showing that the proposed design is effective in the studied settings.
watch_item: Conditional-KL calibration may be sensitive to how groups are sampled and how reward coefficients are estimated, so implementation details could affect stability and reproducibility.
paper_title: When KL Regularization Misfires in Group Policy Optimization
